votes.reason: Unchanged apart from status. The replay is versioned and complete, has no effect endpoint, counts refused inputs explicitly, and recorded timers cannot qualify native deadlines. Both scenarios follow from the EARS. Guarded draft only.

V2 separates capacity refusal from the original operation's outcome. Refusal clears only through proof-safe reclamation, and scope floors retire only through certified retirement or equivalent retained proof. The expired-replay scenario now keeps retained Unknown unchanged and separate from definitive refusal. On the UX side, a capacity refusal is a distinct reportable state, which fits ADOPT-011.

Unchanged. Checkpoint validation comes before admission, Unknown is reconciled without replay, original deadlines are kept, and a coherent checkpoint is not treated as proof that an action completed. Both scenarios are supported by the EARS.

My v1 objection is resolved. The scenario now asserts only equivalence under the correct dependency revision. Performance is measured separately for the adoption decision, and the guardrail says equivalence alone does not justify enabling the cache. The identity-reuse scenario keeps stale family/preview authority out.

Every field must now be either mapped or explicitly reviewed as quotient/stutter/ghost. Quotients preserve authentication, clock and outcome meaning. The new unlisted-field-mutation scenario makes coverage falsifiable. All three scenarios are consistent with the EARS and guardrails.

My v1 wording concern about foreign input is resolved. Rejected input yields only a bounded allowlisted diagnostic, with no settlement and no fabricated Refused outcome. The authenticated-historical-reconciliation scenario correctly limits settlement to the historical obligation, grants nothing to the replacement binding, and renews no deadline. Terminal Refused requires exact evidence or a validated unsent certificate.

Prerequisites are now protocol-specific, need authenticated evidence, and native authority revalidates incarnation, generation and dependency revision at commit. A window Committed receipt cannot stand in for preview drain or presentation. Both scenarios remain supported.

The EARS now covers rejection: a non-conforming event is refused without any authority, ownership or settlement effect, and a bounded diagnostic is kept. Reachability is protocol-specific, per the coordinator correction. The scenarios are consistent.

Unchanged. It applies the conservation-including-admission/transfer correction, and Cancel/Release emission is not retirement. The held-reader scenario keeps fetch revocation separate from terminal release.

The tradeoffs now state that frontend timers may give feedback or withdraw unsent local intent fail-closed, but cannot authorize, extend, settle or time native work. That matches the existing local choice-deadline pattern and INTERACTION.md feedback rules. The scenarios are unchanged and supported.

Reviewed text comes from a catalog that supports localization, with no translation release gate. Unknown stays perceivable and cannot be fabricated as Refused. Both scenarios are supported. As I said in v1, Unknown visibility must not be displaced by later informational status. The guardrail covers that.

ERR-02-02 now separates unauthorized or unrelated receipts (no update) from exact authenticated historical evidence (may reconcile retained Unknown through the declared route), with no deadline change. The guardrail still requires delivery to a qualified AT-active document or a declared native/fallback route, including when an application holds focus. That covers my Orca inactive-document finding, but the route remains an open research and policy freeze; GTK3 has no native announce API. ERR-02-01 is consistent with one-owner deduplication.

Secrets, drafts and pixels are always excluded under ELM-DEL-017. Raw bodies, titles, arguments and paths are excluded by the ordinary allowlist, and any other mode needs a separate contract. It now maps to the actual QA-021/023 and REV-020/021 budget contract. The scenarios are supported.

ERR-04-02 now says each affected operation's original deadline is unchanged and not renewed by recovery. Restored availability is reported separately from unresolved history. Original restore38/recovery34 remain the oracle.

I agree with keeping it a deferred conditional draft. Local export is not selected and must not become a mandatory release blocker. If it is selected later, its review surface also inherits the ELM-UI-009/ELM-UX-023 keyboard/AT obligations.

My v1 objection is resolved. The state-driven EARS now dispatches admitted keyboard or assistive activation only to the native AT-exposed focused identity. The focus-without-publication scenario directly falsifies the hazard I found in source, where Enter resolves the selected row (Surface.elm:154) while keyboard-context admission trusts activeElement. The guardrail says selection is distinct from focus and defers disabled-focusable behavior to the ADOPT-030 policy. All three scenarios are supported. Keyed DOM is still only an implementation choice.

My v1 objection is resolved. Scenario 1 now asserts only identical refusal state on the same control identity, and leaves the announcement count to ADOPT-012. The new stable-name-state-change scenario captures name-equals-visible-label while state and description change, consistent with the UIA Name guidance and KDE Task.qml evidence. The guardrail requires cross-surface relationships to be verified in the native AT tree rather than as DOM idrefs across WebViews.

Unchanged duplicate of ELM-UI-012/UX-028 with stronger evidence packaging. Remaining-work V2 now requires actual-field evidence from S12 on the same tuple. Fixtures should still cover the native GDK key-proof path, which runs before WebKit IM filtering (shared-context.h:52-123), as well as the DOM path. That is an evidence-scope note, not a textual blocker. Both scenarios are supported.

Unchanged. Thresholds are frozen before qualification, and native bounds and reachability are not inferred from CSS or screenshots. S02 V2 now lists contrast, target, focus and reflow freezing. The scenarios are supported.

The dependency-domain wording, the unrelated-observation-refresh scenario and the same-control-during-pending scenario (no second intent, one truthful not-accepted result, no announcement storm) are supported and match ELM-UI-007/015. On interpretation, I read 'never queue, defer or automatically replay input not accepted in that state' as excluding native ordered control events that the native control lane does accept, such as release-before-readiness and Escape under INTERACTION.md:29. I record that reading as a non-blocking note rather than forcing a change.

Unchanged. Stages are labelled separately, and physical completion comes only from identity-matched native evidence. Both scenarios are supported. Accessible feedback should be traced as its own feedback stage under ADOPT-024.

The close-during-reservation scenario now keeps the closed demand cancelled with its owner and cleanup recorded. Other demand may use only independently available capacity, never the held reservation before matching release. This is consistent with cancellation not being retirement.

Unchanged. A live reduced-motion change settles the existing transaction without replay or deadline reset, per INTERACTION.md:45. The successor derives from native last-presented geometry. The switch policy is still to be frozen.

Unchanged. Budgets are frozen, missing stages are declared, observer overhead is separated, and no numbers are invented. Under the missing-stage rule, accessible-feedback latency must be either measured or explicitly declared missing, which satisfies my v1 note.
Unchanged. Proof IDs are not delivery ordinals, idempotent Ack retry is preserved, and there is no global total order. The scenarios are supported.

Unchanged. An over-budget route is rejected in favor of a truthful unavailable state, without closing source-stop/family gates. Remaining-work V2 makes its S02 measurement row conditional on separate adoption. The unavailable state should be exposed on the control, consistent with 017/028.

V2 adds frozen pacing, a bounded latest-revision limited to native-tracked root-surface commits, and no subsurface/family fidelity expansion. The continuous-change scenario explicitly keeps original deadlines unrenewed and measures impact under 026. Consistent with the follow-up correction.

Unchanged. Source liveness, captured revision and frame age stay distinct. S09 V2 now carries the stale-pixel prohibition. The current captions ('Live preview', 'Client content') need this review, with state on the control and imagery staying inert.

My UXA-02 is preserved: native keyboard and AT focus (not DOM-only), a bounded scope, lock-inert, no mandated EXCLUSIVE mode or new default chord, and declared focus-only versus activation history. Re-prioritizing to existing-phase P5 with early feasibility only is acceptable and matches P5-ELM-UX-023. The source finding still stands: bar KEYBOARD_MODE_NONE (shared-host.c:325) and ungated focus-return to bar DOM (host.c:624). Early feasibility should therefore precede claims that W07 focus-return reaches the bar natively. Both scenarios are supported.

The EARS was corrected to 'expose disabled state and any reason required by the frozen per-surface policy', and RC-006/017/018 were added as related amendment IDs. Scenario 'supported-disabled-action' still says 'native AT exposes unavailable state and reason' unconditionally. That contradicts the corrected EARS. It would also force a reason for state-table disables that have no meaningful user-facing reason, such as Restore on an ordinary window under RC-006. This is the unresolved remainder of my v1 objection. Scenario 'all-disabled-and-focus-retirement' is supported.
requiredChanges: In scenario 'supported-disabled-action', change THEN 'native AT exposes unavailable state and reason' to 'native AT exposes unavailable state and any reason required by the frozen per-surface policy'.

philosophy.reason: Technically faithful to the converged design. Both of my v1 suggestions are incorporated. Principle 5 now keeps selection and focus as distinct states, and Principle 6 says announcements reach the user once under the frozen attention policy without moving focus. Principle 2 now holds native facts as read-only observations of native authority. Principle 4 adds refused/cancelled and reconcile-before-anything. Principle 9 adds proof-safe reclamation and the diagnostics exclusions. The principles still drive concrete decisions: 3 for 021/026/028, 5 for 016, 7 for 009/027, 8 for the 029/030 policy freezes. It claims no release gate and no superiority. 'Aletheia' is an editorial working name; my vote endorses technical fidelity, not the name.

remainingWork.reason: All three of my v1 required changes are addressed. Final-evidence dependencies now bind S04 to S12 actual-field IME evidence (ELM-UI-012/UX-028) and S07 to S12 for ELM-UI-010 surfaces with single-owner AT deduplication, and they are kept separate from the unchanged build sequence. The RC row shows the separate 24/48 amendment. Gate text is declared normative and incorporated verbatim into each ELM-CLOSE EARS. The counts are preserved: S01-S16 230/405 plus C00-C06 12/12 = 242/417. Also preserved: preview 13, restore38/recovery34, case-34, drag/resize52, the 12 W-items and 44 findings. S02 now freezes contrast/target/focus/reflow and context timing/geometry before evaluation, with no invented numbers. The 026/027 rows are conditional on separate adoption. No new product features are added.

disagreements: ADOPT-030: one scenario still requires an unconditional 'reason', contradicting the corrected conditional EARS. This is my only remaining blocking textual correction.

ADOPT-020 (non-blocking interpretation): I read 'never queue, defer or automatically replay input not accepted in that state' as not covering native ordered control events that the native chord/control lane accepts (release-before-readiness, Escape; INTERACTION.md:29). If other reviewers read it otherwise, a one-line guardrail clarification would be needed.

ADOPT-029 (non-blocking, priority): I accept the P5 placement. My earlier view stands that feasibility of native bar keyboard focus should be checked early, because W07 P0 focus-return effects currently target a bar surface that cannot hold keyboard focus.

ADOPT-030 (retained soft preference, non-blocking): as the original author I still recommend that menus and jump lists keep disabled items focusable (APG, Windows parity), while accepting that the per-surface freeze is a policy decision and GTK3's skip convention is defensible.
summary: Final ratification by opus-04-ux-ui-accessibility: 28 accept, 1 refine (ADOPT-030), and ADOPT-015 kept deferred as a conditional export. My v1 blocking corrections to 004, 016 and 017, and all three remaining-work items, are resolved in the V2 bytes. The ADOPT-030 EARS was corrected, but one of its scenarios still carries the old unconditional 'reason' wording; that is my only open blocking item and needs a one-phrase scenario change. I reviewed every scenario, including the new ones: 005 unlisted-field-mutation, 006 authenticated-historical-reconciliation, 016 focus-without-publication, 017 stable-name-state-change, 020 unrelated-observation-refresh and same-control-during-pending, and 027 continuous-change-and-final-revision. I found no other claim unsupported by its EARS or guardrails. Accept means guarded draft contract only, with no conditional mechanism selected. This is not native, AT, IME or release acceptance, and not a mandatory baseline expansion. 242/417, RC24/48, closure 24, preview 13, 38/34/52 and original deadlines, native authority, no Unknown replay and conditional compositor scope are preserved. I echoed the supplied hashes without recomputing them, because no hashing tool was available in this session. These are my votes only; I claim no agreement on behalf of other reviewers, and my dissent is retained.
